mbm-1726.clue: Listen to the skis before breakfast.
mbm-1726.quote: I took the first lift up on my birthday. The corduroy snow under my skis made a sound like a zipper. At the lodge my little brother zipped my jacket and said, “Another run?”

mbm-1727.clue: I found a whole friendship on page thirty.
mbm-1727.quote: An old used novel had two people's checkers game pencilled in the margin. I set the final position on my board at home. I think the player with the green pencil was about to win.

mbm-1728.clue: Can a wren have a favorite mug?
mbm-1728.quote: I put a chipped cup on the windowsill to hold pencils. By Wednesday there was a dry leaf in it. On Thursday I caught the wren choosing curtains.

mbm-1729.clue: I know the spare by the color of my fingers.
mbm-1729.quote: The alley used to stamp a purple star on your thumb for a spare. The stamp dried up years ago. Mum still brings her purple pencil and draws mine herself.

mbm-1730.clue: Ask me who modeled for the yellow patch.
mbm-1730.quote: My son's first drawing of our yellow cat filled the whole page. I copied every wild proportion into his quilt. He holds the actual cat up to measure how much growing she's got left.

mbm-1731.clue: The tent door makes a very good cinema.
mbm-1731.quote: Camped under an oak, we watched our lantern throw six beetle shadows onto the canvas. My sister whispered dialogue for the smallest one. That beetle had a lot of opinions about breakfast.

mbm-1732.clue: I leave the fancy compass at home for this trail.
mbm-1732.quote: My grandfather drew the route on the inside of his old biscuit tin. Every bend is labeled with something he ate there. We got to the cheese sandwich just after noon.

mbm-1733.clue: I spent less on the frame than the bus ride.
mbm-1733.quote: At a market I found an empty gilt frame. I carried it home around my face, and strangers looked straight through it to admire the buildings. Best guided tour I ever gave.

mbm-1734.clue: I've still got a button from a cinema seat.
mbm-1734.quote: Our old neighborhood cinema replaced its red upholstery. The usher let me take one velvet button from my usual seat. It's on my coat now, two rows below the collar.

mbm-1735.clue: We save a corner for the kettle.
mbm-1735.quote: At breakfast Grandpa leaves one baduk problem set up beside our teapot. I turn the board so the steam clears and move one white stone. That little click starts our morning conversation.

mbm-1736.clue: We name the court after the tide.
mbm-1736.quote: At low tide our beach volleyball court grew a shiny pond along one boundary. The ball came to rest there, perfectly reflected. We all stood still till someone found a camera.

mbm-1737.clue: I know how a bell sounds from underneath.
mbm-1737.quote: On the canal I paddled under the bell tower just as it struck noon. The rings bounced from the bridge into the hollow of my kayak. I put my hand on the deck and felt the last one.

mbm-1738.clue: Our old training shoes get the front row.
mbm-1738.quote: When my first martial arts instructor retired, we lined our battered shoes at the edge of the mat. He recognized his earliest class by the crooked repair on my left toe.

mbm-1739.clue: Mine is the card with the unconvincing moon.
mbm-1739.quote: An ink spot covered the moon on my favorite spell card. My little cousin used a silver sticker to fix it. Now our whole club calls that spell the Baked Potato Eclipse.

mbm-1740.clue: Even the kitchen stool has mittens.
mbm-1740.quote: I crocheted covers for the feet of the stool that scraped our floor. Dad insists on taking them off and lining them up neatly when he mops. Four little green socks in a row.

mbm-1741.clue: We put a mouse behind the cupboard.
mbm-1741.quote: I appliquéd a cabinet on a kitchen quilt. My mother slipped a little gray mouse beneath its openable fabric door. Only people who've helped us do the dishes know to look.

mbm-1742.clue: I learned to ski with my teeth showing.
mbm-1742.quote: I held my breath every time I crossed the wake. The boat driver started wearing a felt moustache with his sunglasses. I couldn't pass him without laughing, which took care of the breathing problem.

mbm-1743.clue: Save the short yellow piece for the end.
mbm-1743.quote: My first crochet hat ran out of blue a row before the crown. I finished with yellow and my nephew said the sun was coming up. Now everyone orders a sunrise.

mbm-1744.clue: I've hidden a whole afternoon in a pocket.
mbm-1744.quote: I made a travel quilt from maps printed on fabric. Under a little flap at the lake I stitched two crooked paddles and our first canoe trip's date. Mum lifted the flap and called shotgun.

mbm-1745.clue: My notebook has a waiting room.
mbm-1745.quote: I cut a pocket into the back cover for characters who don't fit the chapter yet. The one with the red umbrella waited three months. The first time I wrote a storm she was out in a flash.

mbm-1746.quote: I built a greenhouse out of clear kit sprue and parked my tiny gardener mecha outside it. Each week I move the model's watering can to whatever seedling has come up overnight.

mbm-1747.clue: My costume has a very dramatic pocket.
mbm-1747.quote: I played a waiter with two lines. On opening night an actor missed his cue and I found a folded paper menu in my apron. I read every special until he arrived, to thunderous applause for the soup.

mbm-1748.clue: That little windmill and I have an understanding.
mbm-1748.quote: My niece chose the quietest moment to putt. Just as the blade paused, a moth landed on it. She waited for the moth to finish resting. The whole group behind us waited too.

mbm-1749.clue: I have to put the laundry away before I practice.
mbm-1749.quote: I learned to juggle with rolled socks. Now that I can keep three in the air, Mum tosses me unmatched ones while she sorts. I still drop everything when a pair finally meets.

mbm-1750.clue: Nobody's drawn my favorite landmark on the map.
mbm-1750.quote: The guide pointed up at the clock tower. I looked down at a brass fish set into the pavement, polished shiny by decades of shoes. The clock was fine. I went back twice for the fish.
